name: nyc-tlc-hvfhv-data-pipeline
what_it_holds: Python/DuckDB/GeoPandas/Streamlit pipeline built specifically on NYC TLC's High-Volume For-Hire-Vehicle (Uber/Lyft/Via/Juno) trip-record dataset, described as analyzing 'millions of rideshare trips'.
why_useful: A second, independent pipeline confirming the official TLC HVFHV rideshare dataset (distinct table from yellow/green taxi) is easily machine-pullable; useful if the team wants ride-hail-specific volumes (as opposed to taxi) split out for airport/ground-travel demand reads.
time_coverage: not specified in listing; TLC HVFHV data runs 2019-present
duplicate_of_holding: overlaps with toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data's FHV coverage, but isolates the HVFHV table specifically
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: A second, independent pipeline confirming the official TLC HVFHV rideshare dataset (distinct table from yellow/green taxi) is easily machine-pullable; useful if the team wants ride-hail-specific volumes (as opposed to taxi) split out for airport/ground-travel demand reads.

name: amtrak (amtrak.js / amtraker)
what_it_holds: NPM/JS client for the community api.amtraker.com API: live Amtrak train GPS positions, speed/heading, station metadata, and planned vs. actual arrival/departure (real-time only, no history stored in the repo).
why_useful: Could support a rolling on-time-performance / delay-frequency scrape as a service-quality or disruption proxy for Amtrak, complementing piemadd/amtrak-data's monthly financial tables with finer-grained (per-train) timing data, but requires building the historical archive yourself.
license: Open Data Commons Attribution License (data); repo code licence separate
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Could support a rolling on-time-performance / delay-frequency scrape as a service-quality or disruption proxy for Amtrak, complementing piemadd/amtrak-data's monthly financial tables with finer-grained (per-train) timing data, but requires building the historical archive yourself.

name: nyc-citibike-data
what_it_holds: Scripts to download and analyze NYC Citi Bike system trip data (bike-share) and load into PostgreSQL, from Citi Bike's own public trip-history exports.
why_useful: Tangential ground-mobility/local-tourism-activity proxy (bike-share usage correlates with short-trip/tourist foot traffic in NYC); marginal fit to the rail/rideshare theme but a real, maintained dataset method worth noting for completeness.
size_hint: tens of millions of trip rows (external)
last_activity: companion repo to nyc-taxi-data, periodically maintained
themes: Rail and ground travel: Amtrak ridership, SNCF/DB/Trenitalia open data, Eurostar, bus (FlixBus), rideshare datasets (Uber Movement), NYC TLC airport trips, Chicago taxi
why_all: Tangential ground-mobility/local-tourism-activity proxy (bike-share usage correlates with short-trip/tourist foot traffic in NYC); marginal fit to the rail/rideshare theme but a real, maintained dataset method worth noting for completeness.

name: north-america-border-crossing-dashboard
duplicate_of_holding: same underlying data.gov BTS Border Crossing Entry Data series as AlexBogden/canadian-border-crossings-analysis above, packaged only as a Power BI file rather than raw CSV
what_it_holds: dashboard.pbix (Power BI file, hosted on Google Drive due to size) built on the data.gov 'Border Crossing Entry Data' series, covering US-Canada and US-Mexico borders 1996-2025 by state/port; MIT license; 2 commits
why_useful: Confirms the BTS Border Crossing Entry Data series (1996-2025, both US-Canada and US-Mexico, state/port level) as a public, easily citable source, though this particular repo does not commit the raw CSV itself (only a Power BI binary on Google Drive) so it's lower priority than the AlexBogden repo above.
geography: US-Canada and US-Mexico borders, all states
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
why_all: Confirms the BTS Border Crossing Entry Data series (1996-2025, both US-Canada and US-Mexico, state/port level) as a public, easily citable source, though this particular repo does not commit the raw CSV itself (only a Power BI binary on Google Drive) so it's lower priority than the AlexBogden repo above.

name: nakordoni developer API docs
what_it_holds: OpenAPI spec + code samples for nakordoni.eu's commercial API: real-time and historical border-queue lengths/wait estimates at European (mostly Ukraine-EU and intra-EU) truck/car checkpoints, ML 24h/7d queue forecasts, hourly/daily historical stats per checkpoint, plus adjacent European fuel-price, POI, road-condition and toll data; sourced from national road authorities, TomTom/HERE, crowd reports; free-tier requires email registration; last touched 2026-09-13
why_useful: A live, queryable proxy for European land-border friction/congestion (crossing wait times) that could stand in for cross-border travel intensity in EMEA, complementing Schengen visa-issuance stats; only useful as a 'method' pointer since actual queue data lives behind their API, not committed to the repo.
geography: Europe, primarily Ukraine-EU and intra-EU checkpoints
time_coverage: live + historical stats per checkpoint (span not specified)
themes: Cross-border and visa data: Schengen visa statistics, ESTA, ETIAS, CBP wait times, passport index, border crossings BTS
why_all: A live, queryable proxy for European land-border friction/congestion (crossing wait times) that could stand in for cross-border travel intensity in EMEA, complementing Schengen visa-issuance stats; only useful as a 'method' pointer since actual queue data lives behind their API, not committed to the repo.
